sections.title: Search intent, captured. One goal: your calendar, full.

items.title: High-intent searches: clients with a credit card in hand
items.body:
Google Ads is demand capture, not demand creation. Nobody searches “fractional CO2 laser Dubai price” out of idle curiosity — these are clients at the end of their decision, comparing two or three clinics. Winning that click means winning the booking, often the same week.

That’s also why beauty CPCs are worth paying: a click costing a few dirhams that becomes a laser hair removal package, and then a repeat client, is one of the cheapest acquisitions in your business — when the account is run with discipline. Because happy salon and clinic clients rebook, the real return isn’t that first click — it’s the lifetime value it unlocks.

sections.title: Where your ad budget actually goes

items.title: Wasted spend: where salon ad budgets actually go
items.body:
In audits of beauty accounts we consistently find a large slice of the budget doing nothing: clicks from searchers looking for training courses, at-home devices, jobs, or treatments in the wrong emirate. One missing negative keyword list can quietly cost more than an agency fee.

The second leak is structural: one campaign, one ad, all treatments mixed together — so Google’s Quality Score drops, your cost per click rises, and neither Smart Bidding nor you can tell which searches actually book.

sections.title: Google Ads, tailored for every beauty business
sections.intro: Your campaigns adapt to how your specific business books clients — walk-ins, consultations, packages or deposit-required treatments.

items.title: How much should I budget for Google Ads?
items.text: As a planning range (Glowth estimate), many UAE salons and clinics start from AED 3,000–6,000/month in ad spend; multi-treatment aesthetic clinics often run AED 8,000–15,000/month. That's separate from our Google Ads management fee (our Dubai beauty marketing cost guide breaks this down) — your free audit gives an exact number for both, based on your treatments and area, not a generic rule of thumb.

items.title: Google Ads or Instagram Ads first?
items.text: Google Ads wins for high-intent, ready-to-book searches like "botox price abu dhabi." Instagram ads win for discovery and brand-building. Most clinics run both — we typically start with Google Ads for the fastest measurable return, then layer in Instagram.

items.title: Can aesthetic clinics advertise injectables at all?
items.text: Carefully. Google's Healthcare & medicines policy restricts prescription-drug terms in ads, keywords and landing pages, and UAE law bars advertising prescription-only medicines to the public — so ads promote the consultation or treatment category (e.g. "anti-wrinkle consultation"), not the drug brand. Healthcare ads may also need approval from the local regulator — DHA in Dubai, DoH in Abu Dhabi, the relevant health authority elsewhere. We write ad copy and landing pages with both sets of rules in mind from day one to minimise disapprovals.

items.title: Do you run Google Maps and Performance Max ads too?
items.text: Yes — where it fits, we add Performance Max (with your Google Business Profile linked) for Maps calls and direction taps, alongside Search. (Google's Local Services Ads aren't currently available in the UAE.) For local beauty businesses, Maps visibility is often where the cheapest bookings come from. For bilingual clinics, we also run Arabic-language campaigns targeting the meaningful share of UAE searchers who query in Arabic first.

items.title: What's a "money keyword" vs a wasted click?
items.text: Money keywords are treatment + city or "near me" searches from someone ready to book ("laser hair removal dubai marina"). Wasted clicks come from broad match terms like "laser hair removal course" or "at home laser device" — searches with zero booking intent that a proper negative keyword list blocks from day one. See our keyword guides for salon Google Ads and clinic Google Ads.

items.title: Who owns the Google Ads account?
items.text: You do, always. The account is created under your own Google Ads login, not ours — full transparency and no lock-in. Monthly reports show exactly what each dirham earned, traced to a booking, not just a click.

sections.title: Glowth vs. a typical agency
sections.footnote: Most Google Ads agencies, generalist PPC companies and marketing providers run every industry through the same playbook. As a beauty-only Google Ads agency, we skip that — and the winning setup isn’t ads or SEO alone, it’s paid ads buying today’s bookings while organic search compounds underneath without a per-click cost.

sections.title: Google Ads for salons & clinics — before you ask

items.q: How long until Google Ads produces bookings?
items.a: Google Ads typically produces bookings within 2–4 weeks of launch. SEO takes longer to compound (3–6 months) but becomes your lowest-cost channel long term — running both together is usually the fastest path to a full calendar.

items.q: Do you target every treatment we offer?
items.a: No — a tightly focused set of “money keywords” for your top 3–5 treatments outperforms a broad account every time. We’d rather own page one for the searches that book than spread thin across everything you offer.

items.q: Who manages the account day to day?
items.a: As your Google Ads specialist, we manage the account, but you keep full ownership and access at all times. Weekly optimisation sprints — bids, budgets, search terms — are handled by our Google Ads experts on our end; you just watch the cost-per-booking number improve.

items.q: Can ads connect to our booking system?
items.a: Yes — every ad connects to a per-treatment landing page with call tracking, WhatsApp click-to-chat, and form tracking wired directly into your booking system, so every dirham spent is traced back to an actual appointment.

items.q: What exactly am I paying for?
items.a: Your ad spend (paid directly to Google, not to us), plus a management fee for strategy, campaign builds and weekly optimisation. Both are itemised separately before you commit — no hidden markup on your media budget.
